question: Dizygotic (fraternal) twins are formed when:

options.A: Two separate eggs are fertilized by two separate sperm
options.B: A single fertilized egg splits into two parts
options.C: An unfertilized egg divides spontaneously
options.D: One egg is fertilized simultaneously by two different sperm

explanation: That's correct! Fraternal twins happen when the ovaries release two eggs, and both get fertilized independently. Think of them as brothers and sisters born at the exact same time!

question: A bedridden patient has a red spot on their lower back that doesn't fade when pressed. As a nurse, what should you do first?

options.A: Implement a strict turning schedule and use a pressure-relieving surface
options.B: Restrict daily fluid intake to reduce local tissue edema
options.C: Apply strong antiseptic ointment directly over the red skin area
options.D: Massaged the reddened spot vigorously to stimulate blood flow

explanation: That red spot is an early pressure ulcer warning! Taking the pressure off by turning the patient is your best first move.

question: At what point in pregnancy do the very first structures of the nervous system start to form?

options.A: During the final trimester
options.B: During the third week of pregnancy
options.C: Around the fifth month of gestation
options.D: Immediately after birth

explanation: Spot on! Nervous system development starts super early—during the third week of pregnancy—which is why early antenatal care is so important.

question: What is the main job of international health organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: Setting local hospital staffing wages across individual states
options.B: Punishing nurses who fail bedside board examinations
options.C: Directing international health and managing global health security
options.D: Running private clinics in major capital cities

explanation: You got it! The WHO helps coordinate responses to global health crises and sets international standards that keep the whole world safer.

question: Why might someone feel dizzy or carsick if they try to read a book inside a moving car?

options.A: The eyes and the inner ear send conflicting signals to the brain.
options.B: The brainstem shuts down the vestibular nuclei temporarily.
options.C: The proprioceptors in the neck freeze from lack of movement.
options.D: The visual cortex stops receiving oxygen from the carotid arteries.

explanation: Motion sickness happens when your eyes say "I'm sitting still reading," but your inner ear says "We are moving fast!" Confusion leads to that dizzy feeling. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h7)

question: When should the nurse stop the repeating cycles of fluid instillation and drainage during a gastric lavage?

options.A: When the collection bucket is half filled with fluid
options.B: When exactly one hour has passed on the clock
options.C: When the returned lavage fluid runs completely clear
options.D: When the patient asks for a glass of cold water

explanation: The wash cycles continue until the fluid coming back out is completely clear of toxins, pills, or debris, indicating the stomach is empty. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h5)

question: Which of these structures sits right inside the vaginal vestibule?

options.A: Fallopian tube ampulla
options.B: Uterine fundus
options.C: Ovarian follicle
options.D: External urethral opening

explanation: Well done! The vestibule is the space where both the opening for urine (urethra) and the vagina are located.

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with thick, sticky mucus blocking their airways and causing severe coughing. Which type of nebulized medication is most appropriate?

options.A: A local anesthetic
options.B: A beta-blocker
options.C: A mucolytic agent
options.D: An intravenous fluid

explanation: Mucolytics specifically target and break down thick pulmonary secretions, making them easier for the patient to expel. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h2)

question: Why might a doctor order a transvaginal ultrasound instead of a transabdominal one?

options.A: It allows visualization of the entire abdomen including the liver and stomach
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any patient preparation or consent
options.C: It is completely painless and causes zero discomfort for all patients
options.D: It places the transducer closer to the pelvic organs for clearer images

explanation: Spot on! Slipping the probe into the vaginal canal brings it right next to the uterus and ovaries, giving us a much sharper picture than scanning through the tummy wall.

question: Why are elderly patients at a much higher risk for drug buildup and toxicity?

options.A: They produce more stomach acid, which alters how drugs are absorbed.
options.B: Their natural decline in kidney and liver function slows down drug clearance.
options.C: They consume more fluids, which dilutes the medication in their blood.
options.D: Their body fat decreases significantly, trapping water-soluble drugs.

explanation: As people age, filtering organs like the kidneys and liver naturally slow down. This makes it harder for older adults to clear drugs at a normal rate, so we adjust doses carefully.

question: What is a major root cause of unwanted pregnancies that lead to unsafe abortions?

options.A: Universal access to emergency birth control pills
options.B: Unmet needs and lack of access to modern contraceptives
options.C: Mandatory sex education classes in all primary schools
options.D: Excessive availability of free family planning clinics

explanation: When people cannot get or afford reliable birth control, unplanned pregnancies happen more often. Patient education is our best tool here!

question: Which type of feedback mechanism is most common for maintaining normal daily physiological ranges?

options.A: Negative feedback
options.B: Neutral feedback
options.C: Additive feedback
options.D: Positive feedback

explanation: Negative feedback is the most common control mechanism because it counteracts deviations to keep body systems stable. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why is putting in a large-bore intravenous (IV) line such an urgent priority when managing severe PPH?

options.A: To provide a pathway for total parenteral nutrition
options.B: To make it easy to give routine pain relief
options.C: To allow rapid running of IV fluids and blood products
options.D: To monitor central venous pressure continuously

explanation: When a mother is losing blood quickly, every second counts. Wide IV lines let you pump in lifesaving fluids and blood fast enough to beat shock.

question: Why is it so important to rinse the hair thoroughly after shampooing?

options.A: Leftover soap residue can cause scalp irritation and dryness
options.B: Unrinsed shampoo actively accelerates hair follicle growth
options.C: Remaining soap prevents the hair from absorbing water
options.D: Residue permanently changes the natural color of the hair

explanation: Leaving soap behind can dry out the skin and make the scalp itchy and flaky. A good rinse keeps your patient comfortable! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why do our hands and face get a much larger area on the sensory homunculus than our back or thighs?

options.A: They are closer physically to the brain
options.B: They contain larger bones and thicker muscles
options.C: They receive more blood flow from the carotid arteries
options.D: They have a much higher density of sensory receptors

explanation: Spot on! Areas of the body we use for fine, detailed feeling (like fingertips and lips) have way more receptors, so the brain gives them extra processing space.

question: When should you choose sterile surgical gloves instead of regular exam gloves?

options.A: When performing a procedure inside a sterile body cavity
options.B: During routine physical checks on unbroken skin
options.C: Whenever touching a patient with an infection
options.D: When cleaning up a blood spill on the floor

explanation: Whenever you enter a sterile space or use sterile instruments, you need sterile gloves to keep bacteria out. You've got this!

question: What is the primary purpose of advance care planning?

options.A: To allow patients to state their medical wishes before they lose decision-making capacity
options.B: To reduce hospital liability in case of accidental patient falls
options.C: To guarantee that a patient receives aggressive life support under all circumstances
options.D: To transfer financial assets to family members before passing away

explanation: Advance care planning lets individuals guide their future healthcare treatment when they are no longer able to speak or make decisions for themselves. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h6)

question: As a nurse, how must you make sure the traction weights are positioned during your shift?

options.A: They are adjusted upward by the patient
options.B: They are hidden beneath heavy wool blankets
options.C: They rest securely on the foot of the bed
options.D: They hang freely without touching the floor

explanation: Always check those weights! If they touch the floor, they lose their pulling power and the therapy won't work.

question: Which of these is NOT a common feature of end-of-life care in Nigeria?

options.A: Involvement of extended family in medical discussions
options.B: Widespread legal use of formal living wills and advance directives
options.C: Strong influence of Christian and Islamic religious beliefs
options.D: Strict criminal prohibitions against assisted suicide and euthanasia

explanation: While family involvement, religion, and strict laws against euthanasia are very common in Nigeria, formal written living wills are still not widely used or legally integrated into everyday hospital practice yet.

question: What makes probability sampling special?

options.A: Every member of the population has a known chance of being selected
options.B: The researcher hand-picks individuals who fit a specific profile
options.C: Only patients with severe symptoms are included in the study
options.D: Participants are chosen based on their easy availability to the nurse

explanation: Spot on! Probability sampling uses fairness and random selection, meaning everyone in the group has a fair shot at being chosen.

question: What is the main difference between cleaning and sanitizing a kitchen surface?

options.A: Cleaning uses chemical agents, while sanitizing only uses plain water.
options.B: Cleaning is done after food prep, while sanitizing is done before food prep.
options.C: Cleaning kills all bacteria, while sanitizing only removes visible grease.
options.D: Cleaning removes dirt and food, while sanitizing reduces microorganisms to safe levels.

explanation: Spot on! Cleaning washes away visible dirt and food, while sanitizing goes after the invisible germs using heat or chemicals.

question: What is the main job of the Theatre Sterile Supply Unit (TSSU)?

options.A: Disposing of hazardous biological waste from wards
options.B: Manufacturing single-use surgical equipment
options.C: Processing, sterilizing, and distributing medical instruments
options.D: Conducting pre-surgery patient assessments

explanation: You've got this! The TSSU is the heartbeat behind every clean surgery. Its main job is to safely clean, sterilize, and hand out surgical tools so patients stay infection-free.

question: Why are private discussions during home visits particularly beneficial for women's health assessments?

options.A: They prevent family members from ever asking questions about medications.
options.B: They legally replace the need for any laboratory blood testing.
options.C: They help women feel comfortable discussing sensitive issues like domestic safety.
options.D: They ensure the patient will never experience chronic illness.

explanation: Privacy builds confidence, allowing patients to safely share private health concerns, mental struggles, or safety risks at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h7)

question: Which type of isolation is used to protect a patient with a very weak immune system?

options.A: Strict contact isolation
options.B: Respiratory isolation
options.C: Protective isolation
options.D: Standard isolation

explanation: Protective or reverse isolation guards patients who cannot fight off everyday germs by keeping outside microorganisms away from them. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: Which pregnancy hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing the valve between the stomach and food pipe?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body to make room for baby, which also loosens the sphincter keeping stomach acid down.

question: An order calls for 500 mg of Paracetamol. The available tablets are 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?

options.A: 2 tablets
options.B: 1 tablet
options.C: 0.5 tablet
options.D: 4 tablets

explanation: Using the formula: (500 mg / 250 mg) × 1 tablet = 2 tablets. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h4)

question: A clinic manager limits the number of continuous hours a nurse works in a high-radiation department. What type of control is this?

options.A: Engineering control
options.B: Elimination control
options.C: Substitution control
options.D: Administrative control

explanation: When management changes work schedules, policies, or rules to limit your exposure time, they are using administrative controls.

question: How do antiviral medications help male patients who have genital herpes?

options.A: They permanently block all future sexual transmission risks
options.B: They completely eliminate the virus from nerve cells
options.C: They shorten outbreak duration and reduce symptom severity
options.D: They prevent the patient from ever contracting bacterial infections

explanation: Antivirals are great for calming down outbreaks and easing pain, but remember—they manage the virus; they don't cure it completely.

question: Why must breastfeeding mothers make sure they drink plenty of extra fluids every day?

options.A: To replace fluids lost through breastmilk production
options.B: To flush out the kidneys and stop weight gain
options.C: To help the lochia turn white faster
options.D: To prevent the uterus from contracting too fast

explanation: Breastmilk is mostly water! If mom doesn't drink enough, her milk supply can drop and she can easily become dehydrated.

question: What are the main germs responsible for common skin infections like boils and impetigo?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis bacilli
options.B: Staphylococcus and Streptococcus bacteria
options.C: Enteric viruses and parasites
options.D: Dermatophyte fungi and molds

explanation: Staph and Strep are the usual suspects behind those painful, pus-filled skin sores you see so often in clinic rotations.

question: What is the main role of Natural Killer (NK) cells?

options.A: Directly destroy cells infected with viruses or cancer
options.B: Eat up large parasites in the blood
options.C: Make antibodies to fight toxins
options.D: Line the respiratory tract to produce mucus

explanation: Natural Killer cells patrol your body and safely eliminate any of your own cells that have gone rogue or been hijacked by a virus.

question: What is the name of the high-pitched breathing sound heard when a patient has a blocked upper airway?

options.A: Rhonchi
options.B: Crackles
options.C: Wheezing
options.D: Stridor

explanation: That's correct! Stridor is a turbulent, high-pitched sound caused by air rushing through a narrowed upper airway.

question: What is the correct action when a nurse discovers a box of expired intravenous fluids in the treatment room?

options.A: Donate it to a local clinic outside the hospital system
options.B: Use it quickly for non-critical patients before anyone notices
options.C: Hide it at the back of the cupboard until the next audit
options.D: Remove it from the shelf and follow proper waste disposal protocols

explanation: Expired items must be isolated and disposed of safely to ensure they are never accidentally given to a patient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h7)

question: What is the primary male surgical sterilization procedure called?

options.A: Tubal ligation
options.B: Vasectomy
options.C: Orchiectomy
options.D: Prostatectomy

explanation: A vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens tubes to prevent sperm from entering the semen. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which finding is considered a normal, expected temporary side effect following a cystoscopy procedure?

options.A: Mild burning during urination and slight pink-tinged urine
options.B: Inability to feel the need to urinate for several weeks
options.C: Severe lower abdominal pain radiating to the shoulders
options.D: Complete absence of urine output for twenty-four hours

explanation: Passing the scope through the urethra causes minor irritation and mucosal trauma, leading to temporary burning and light bleeding. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which cranial nerves are attached to the medulla oblongata?

options.A: CN V, VI, VII, and VIII
options.B: CN IX, X, XI, and XII
options.C: CN III, IV, V, and VI
options.D: CN I, II, III, and IV

explanation: The glossopharyngeal, vagus, accessory, and hypoglossal cranial nerves all have their roots emerging from the medulla. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h2)

question: What can happen if you use the wrong liquid (diluent) to mix a vaccine?

options.A: It can destroy the vaccine or harm the client
options.B: It doubles the number of active doses inside the vial
options.C: It automatically turns the liquid into a bright blue color
options.D: It extends the expiration date by exactly six months

explanation: Every vaccine has a specific liquid made just for it. Using the wrong one ruins the dose and compromises patient safety.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for someone living with long-term Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Completely restoring lost declarative memories from childhood
options.B: Training the brain to regrow lost neurons through intense puzzles
options.C: Teaching the patient how to fabricate stories more convincingly
options.D: Maximizing remaining functional independence using environmental aids

explanation: Since memory loss sticks around, we focus on helping them stay safe and independent using daily routines, calendars, and friendly cues.

question: What is the primary purpose of decontamination in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To ensure that expired drugs are safely disposed of in the incinerator
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new medical instruments
options.C: To make hospital wards smell fresh and clean for visitors
options.D: To break the chain of infection and protect patients and staff

explanation: Decontamination removes or destroys harmful microorganisms to stop them from spreading to vulnerable patients and healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: How would you explain a negative feedback loop of hormones to a curious patient?

options.A: It allows the brain to control your heart rate and breathing rate simultaneously.
options.B: It prevents the testes from ever changing in size throughout your lifetime.
options.C: It stops the body from producing too much testosterone when levels are already high.
options.D: It ensures that the pituitary gland stops working completely during physical rest.

explanation: Think of it like an air conditioner thermostat! When hormone levels get high enough, a signal goes back to the brain to slow things down so the body doesn't overproduce.

question: What triggers the strong inflammatory flare-up called the Mazzotti reaction during parasite treatment?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the plastic pill capsule
options.B: Sudden dehydration caused by lack of drinking water
options.C: Direct toxic injury to human liver cells by the drug
options.D: The rapid release of proteins from dying microfilariae

explanation: You're doing great! When masses of tiny parasites die off all at once, releasing their proteins into the blood, it sparks a strong immune reaction.

question: An NGO working inside an internally displaced persons (IDP) camp is most likely to provide which service?

options.A: Commercial airline pilot training programs
options.B: Stock market trading classes for displaced adults
options.C: Malnutrition screening and cholera prevention campaigns
options.D: Luxury spa treatments and physical fitness coaching

explanation: Camps often struggle with clean water and food security. Checking for malnutrition and stopping disease outbreaks like cholera are top priorities.

question: What key element is missing from a vague aim statement like 'we will improve patient safety'?

options.A: Detailed medical diagnoses for every patient
options.B: A complete history of past nursing errors
options.C: The signatures of the hospital board of directors
options.D: Specific targets, a timeline, and the target patient group

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Without knowing how much change, by when, and for whom, a team can't measure success.

question: A nurse treats an unemployed mother whose children are malnourished and out of school due to financial hardship. What is the best immediate action for the nurse to take?

options.A: Refer her to social welfare, food assistance, and community support agencies
options.B: Tell her to find a job and send her home immediately
options.C: Wait until her physical health deteriorates further
options.D: Admit all the children into the inpatient medical ward

explanation: Spot on! Referring her to social services provides immediate help for food and family needs alongside basic care. You're thinking like a true nurse! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h7)

question: Which animal is the main natural home for the Lassa fever virus here in Nigeria?

options.A: The domestic dog
options.B: Freshwater snails
options.C: The multimammate rat
options.D: Free-roaming cattle

explanation: Great job! The multimammate rat sheds the Lassa virus in its waste, which can easily contaminate food items in our homes and barns.

question: Oops! A scrubbed nurse accidentally drops their hands below waist level before putting on a gown. What should they do?

options.A: Ask the circulator to spray antiseptic on the hands
options.B: Lift hands back up and start gowning
options.C: Wipe hands quickly with alcohol rub and keep going
options.D: Treat the hands as contaminated and repeat the entire scrub

explanation: Anything below the waist is considered unsafe territory. Better safe than sorry—time for a quick re-scrub!

question: What happens to the blood vessels in the skin when the body needs to cool down?

options.A: They widen to bring warm blood closer to the skin surface
options.B: They thicken their walls to prevent any fluid loss
options.C: They stop carrying blood entirely to save energy
options.D: They narrow to trap heat deep inside the body core

explanation: You got it! Widening these vessels (vasodilation) lets extra body heat escape easily into the cooler air outside.

question: Which patient sensation is commonly reported immediately after receiving a fast IV push of adenosine?

options.A: Severe numbness and tingling in both legs and feet
options.B: A brief feeling of the heart pausing or chest pressure
options.C: Sudden uncontrollable shaking in the hands and arms
options.D: An intense craving for cold water and sweet foods

explanation: Adenosine momentarily stops electrical conduction through the heart, which patients often experience as a frightening pause or thump. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which part of the spinal cord gives rise to the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Lumbar and sacral region
options.B: Craniosacral region
options.C: Thoracolumbar region
options.D: Cervical region only

explanation: Sympathetic fibers emerge from the chest (thoracic) and upper lower-back (lumbar) areas of the spine. That's why we call it the thoracolumbar outflow!

question: What is the primary purpose of breaking any link in the chain of infection?

options.A: To make the patient immune to all known viruses
options.B: To completely sterilize the human skin permanently
options.C: To cure a chronic illness without using antibiotics
options.D: To stop the transmission of infectious diseases

explanation: Interrupting even one link in the chain stops the microbe from reaching a new host and spreading disease. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h1)

question: How do referrals help optimize healthcare resources?

options.A: By stopping the purchase of expensive family planning commodities altogether
options.B: By ensuring that nurses only work one day a week at each health facility
options.C: By forcing all clients to bypass primary centers and go straight to teaching hospitals
options.D: By keeping primary clinics focused on routine care while advanced centers handle complex cases

explanation: Proper referral sorting ensures facilities use their specific staff skills and equipment efficiently without overloading primary centers. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h2)

question: Why can traditional power dynamics sometimes delay medical care for pregnant women?

options.A: Women are legally banned from talking to doctors first.
options.B: Hospitals refuse to treat women without a signed consent form.
options.C: Men always prefer traditional herbs over modern medicine.
options.D: The woman may need to wait for the man's approval and funds.

explanation: When getting care depends entirely on someone else's permission and money, emergencies can worsen while waiting.

question: How does the school use overall performance data from an entire class?

options.A: To spot gaps in the curriculum and update courses
options.B: To decide who gets scholarship money
options.C: To market the school to new applicants
options.D: To cut down the required clinical hours

explanation: When schools look at how everyone scored as a group, they can see if a certain course needs better materials or extra teaching time.

question: Why do doctors often order a full blood count (FBC) for a patient with heavy periods (menorrhagia)?

options.A: To look for a bacterial infection in the uterus
options.B: To see if the patient might get gestational diabetes
options.C: To check the levels of progesterone and estrogen
options.D: To check for low blood iron (anemia) caused by blood loss

explanation: Spot on! Heavy monthly bleeding can slowly drain the body's iron stores, leading to iron-deficiency anemia that needs our nursing care.

question: In Parkinson's disease, which part of the brain is mainly damaged, leading to low dopamine levels?

options.A: Cerebellar cortex
options.B: Substantia nigra
options.C: Medulla oblongata
options.D: Frontal lobe

explanation: You've got this! The substantia nigra is the brain area packed with dopamine-producing cells. When these cells break down, movement problems start to show. Spotting this early helps you understand why Parkinson's affects movement so much!

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to ask a patient to demonstrate how they use their inhaler?

options.A: To check if the patient is strong enough to crush the capsule
options.B: To measure how fast the patient can blow air into a balloon
options.C: To ensure the patient bought the correct brand of medication
options.D: To catch hidden errors that could prevent the medicine from working

explanation: It's easy for patients to pick up little habits over time that stop the medicine from working right. Seeing them do it live is the best way to help them correct it!

question: What is the main sign of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It worsens when the patient sits or stands up
options.B: It disappears completely after eating a meal
options.C: It only affects the left side of the forehead
options.D: It is accompanied by sudden high fever

explanation: Brilliant! When the patient sits up, the low fluid pressure pulls on sensitive head structures—making it hurt worse until they lie flat again.

question: How is the best way to kick off the discussion section?

options.A: By summarizing the primary findings in plain language
options.B: By proposing a brand new theory of human behavior
options.C: By listing every single p-value calculated in the study
options.D: By criticizing the work done by previous authors

explanation: Spot on! Starting with a clear, simple summary reminds your reader of the main scoop before you dive deep into what it all means.

question: Why is palliative care introduced early for patients with inherited degenerative conditions?

options.A: To shorten the overall duration of the chronic disease process
options.B: To transfer complete financial responsibility to the nursing staff
options.C: To immediately stop all medical therapies and disease-specific medications
options.D: To focus on symptom relief and quality of life alongside active treatment

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the very end; it's all about keeping the patient comfortable, happy, and pain-free right from diagnosis.

question: In community health nursing, what is the main goal of advocacy?

options.A: Protecting and promoting the rights and health of vulnerable populations
options.B: Prescribing medications when doctors are unavailable
options.C: Managing hospital financial records and budgets
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital visitation rules

explanation: Spot on! Advocacy is all about being a voice for people and communities who struggle to speak up for themselves, making sure they get the care and respect they deserve.

question: Which of these is classified as a modern contraceptive method?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Withdrawal method
options.C: Periodic abstinence
options.D: Calendar tracking

explanation: Implants are modern medical methods! Methods like withdrawal and tracking the calendar are traditional practices rather than modern medical interventions.

question: What happens when an anticholinergic drug successfully binds to a receptor on the bladder?

options.A: The muscle contracts harder to empty the bladder completely
options.B: Normal muscle contractions are blocked, preventing spasms
options.C: Urine production in the kidneys stops temporarily
options.D: Blood flow to the urinary tract increases significantly

explanation: By occupying the spot, the drug blocks acetylcholine from turning on the squeeze switch, giving the bladder a chance to rest.

question: What type of strong connective tissue attaches skeletal muscles directly to bones?

options.A: Tendon
options.B: Synovium
options.C: Ligament
options.D: Cartilage

explanation: You got it! Tendons connect muscle to bone (remember: 'T'endon = 'T'ies muscle to bone), while ligaments connect bone to bone.

question: Which diagnostic test is primarily used to confirm the location of a suspected ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Routine urinalysis
options.B: Abdominal X-ray scan
options.C: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: A transvaginal ultrasound allows the healthcare provider to look directly inside the uterus and fallopian tubes to see where the pregnancy has implanted. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h5)

question: What is 'elite capture' in the context of community mobilisation?

options.A: When foreign donors pull out all financial support suddenly
options.B: When only wealthy or powerful individuals benefit from or control the project
options.C: When the local police arrest community health workers unjustly
options.D: When traditional healers refuse to speak with modern nurses

explanation: Elite capture happens when powerful community members take over resources meant for everyone. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h7)

question: You just finished dressing a patient's wound with blood-stained gauze. Which bin should this gauze go into?

options.A: Black bin
options.B: Brown bin
options.C: Yellow bin
options.D: Clear bin

explanation: Well done! Blood-soaked materials are considered infectious waste, so they always go into the yellow bin or bag for safe, specialized treatment.

question: What is the main idea behind restorative nursing care for elderly patients?

options.A: To replace physical therapy sessions entirely
options.B: To diagnose new chronic illnesses in older adults
options.C: To provide heavy sedation during painful medical procedures
options.D: To integrate rehabilitation principles into daily nursing routines

explanation: Exactly! Restorative nursing simply means weaving rehab into everyday actions like bathing, eating, and getting out of bed.

question: What determines whether a person is considered Rh-positive?

options.A: The presence of the D antigen on their red blood cells
options.B: The presence of anti-Rh antibodies floating in their plasma
options.C: The presence of both A and B antigens on their platelets
options.D: The total volume of hemoglobin circulating in their blood

explanation: The term Rh-positive simply means the red blood cells carry the D antigen on their outer surface. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why is adaptability so important for nurses working in rural clinics?

options.A: They follow rigid routines that never change
options.B: They often face limited resources and must adjust quickly
options.C: They deal exclusively with surgical trauma cases daily
options.D: They do not need to interact with other health workers

explanation: Correct! Rural clinics often lack heavy equipment and specialized staff, so nurses have to be resourceful and flexible to help their patients.

question: When a dementia patient suddenly acts out or becomes aggressive, what is this most often a sign of?

options.A: A direct side effect of drinking too much water
options.B: A deliberate attempt to upset family members
options.C: An unmet physical need or reaction to distress
options.D: A permanent change in their core personality

explanation: Behavior is communication! When they can't say 'I'm in pain' or 'I'm scared,' they might lash out instead.

question: What is the main danger if a patient suddenly stops taking their daily seizure medication?

options.A: It leads to complete kidney failure and lifelong dialysis needs
options.B: It causes immediate permanent blindness within a few hours
options.C: It results in rapid hair loss and severe skin pigmentation changes
options.D: It can trigger status epilepticus, a dangerous and prolonged seizure state

explanation: Stopping antiseizure drugs abruptly shocks the brain, causing a rebound effect that can trigger severe, continuous seizures (status epilepticus). Patients must always taper under medical advice!

question: How does surveillance help us check if a vaccination campaign worked?

options.A: By calculating the exact salary of the nurses giving the shots
options.B: By showing whether disease rates drop after the vaccines are given
options.C: By tracking how many nurses attended the training workshop
options.D: By testing the chemical composition of vaccine vials

explanation: By keeping track of sickness rates over time, public health teams can easily tell if giving out those vaccines actually stopped the disease.

question: Why do many patients with chronic kidney disease end up developing anemia?

options.A: The spleen removes healthy blood cells prematurely
options.B: The body destroys red blood cells too quickly
options.C: Dietary iron is no longer absorbed in the gut
options.D: Damaged kidneys fail to produce enough erythropoietin

explanation: You're learning fast! Since sick kidneys can't make enough EPO, the bone marrow doesn't get the signal to build new red blood cells, leading to anemia.

question: Why do we often see higher maternal and child mortality rates in rural Nigerian communities compared to big cities?

options.A: Rural populations have a higher birth rate per family
options.B: Rural residents completely reject modern medicine due to cultural laws
options.C: Urban populations have stronger immune systems from birth
options.D: Rural areas have limited access to equipped health facilities and skilled birth attendants

explanation: Spot on! Bad roads, long distances, and lack of well-equipped clinics mean emergencies take too long to reach help. This is why community health nursing is so vital in Nigeria.

question: Which of these findings is completely normal and NOT a sign of heart stress?

options.A: A resting heart rate of 120 beats per minute
options.B: A regular resting pulse rate of 75 beats per minute
options.C: A blood pressure reading consistently above 140/90 mmHg
options.D: An apex beat displaced far to the left of the midclavicular line

explanation: A pulse of 75 bpm sits right in the middle of the normal 60–100 range. Nothing to worry about here! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)

question: What is a common cause of blunt cardiac injury during a motor vehicle accident?

options.A: Inbreathing toxic exhaust fumes from the damaged engine
options.B: The seatbelt cutting directly across the neck muscles
options.C: The driver hitting their chest against the steering wheel
options.D: Sudden exposure to cold air through broken windows

explanation: Direct impact against the steering wheel during rapid deceleration transmits massive blunt force straight through the sternum to the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why is an unsteady walk (gait instability) such a big worry for patients with nerve degeneration?

options.A: It prevents the patient from speaking clearly
options.B: It triggers sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.C: It greatly increases the risk of dangerous falls and injury
options.D: It causes immediate permanent blindness in both eyes

explanation: When balance is off, walking safely becomes a daily challenge. As nurses, keeping our patients safe from falls is a huge priority!

question: What complication can happen if you give an intramuscular injection too low on the back of the hip?

options.A: Lipodystrophy
options.B: Cellulitis of the dermis
options.C: Systemic air embolism
options.D: Sciatic nerve damage

explanation: Watch out for that sciatic nerve! Aiming too low or too close to the middle on the posterior hip can hit this huge nerve, causing terrible pain and walking issues for the patient.

question: A patient on chemo for bone sarcoma has a temperature of 38.5°C and chills. What is your priority nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to put on a heavy sweater and drink hot tea
options.B: Administer a dose of routine oral pain medication for the chills
options.C: Notify the healthcare provider immediately for potential neutropenic sepsis
options.D: Document the finding in the chart and recheck the temperature in six hours

explanation: Chemo lowers white blood cells, making fever a true medical emergency. Always report it right away to protect your patient from sepsis!

question: Why does the idea of 'agency' matter when you are carrying out your daily nursing duties?

options.A: It allows the nurse to change hospital policies without approval.
options.B: It means the nurse is personally exempt from all criminal laws.
options.C: It binds the hospital principal for acts done within employment scope.
options.D: It transfers complete medical licensing rights to the institution.

explanation: As a nurse acting within your normal duties, you represent the hospital. That means your professional actions on the job legally involve the hospital as your principal. Simple and clear!

question: What can happen if you mix certain suspensions with the wrong type of liquid?

options.A: The liquid immediately changes into a bright gas
options.B: The drug becomes twice as potent instantly
options.C: The active drug may precipitate or break down
options.D: The medication turns into a solid plastic block

explanation: Chemical reactions can ruin a drug! Mixing incompatible fluids can cause the medicine to clump up, fall apart, or lose its healing power.

question: What is the main purpose of using a MUAC tape during a health assessment in an IDP camp?

options.A: To measure daily fluid loss from severe diarrhea
options.B: To estimate the total age of an infant accurately
options.C: To check for signs of chronic joint inflammation
options.D: To screen young children for acute malnutrition

explanation: MUAC (Mid-Upper Arm Circumference) is a quick, handy tool nurses use to check if a child is malnourished during emergencies.

question: What should a healthy, newly formed intestinal stoma look like when you check it?

options.A: Pink and moist
options.B: Pale and dry
options.C: Dark purple or black
options.D: Cold and hard

explanation: Great job! A healthy stoma has great blood flow, so it should look pink to red and feel moist. A dark purple or black stoma means trouble with blood supply and is an emergency!

question: When we talk about 'sex' in human health, what are we mainly referring to?

options.A: Physical and physiological traits
options.B: Cultural roles assigned at birth
options.C: Socially constructed behaviors
options.D: Personal expressions of identity

explanation: You've got this! 'Sex' refers to our biological makeup—like chromosomes, hormones, and anatomy—which is different from the social roles we play.

question: Why do economists look at health spending as a percentage of GNP rather than just raw cash amounts?

options.A: It stops inflation from happening in local community pharmacies
options.B: It calculates the exact salary every registered nurse should earn
options.C: It allows fair comparison between countries with different economic sizes and populations
options.D: It predicts the exact number of disease outbreaks in a year

explanation: Using percentages helps us fairly compare health spending between big economies and smaller nations without getting confused by different currency values.

question: What surgical instrument is typically used during a standard laparoscopy for tubal ligation?

options.A: A lighted camera scope and small grasping tools
options.B: A large open abdominal retractor and surgical saw
options.C: A long uterine curette inserted through the vagina
options.D: An ultrasound probe placed directly on the ovaries

explanation: Laparoscopy relies on a small camera inserted via a tiny umbilical incision to guide specialized instruments that seal or block the tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h4)

question: What is the main job of the endocrine system in the body?

options.A: Filtering metabolic waste products out of circulating blood plasma
options.B: Directing immediate, split-second muscle movements and reflexes
options.C: Coordinating slow, sustained processes like growth and metabolism
options.D: Producing physical barriers to protect internal organs from pathogens

explanation: While your nervous system handles quick reflexes (like pulling your hand from a hot stove), the endocrine system takes the long view—slowly and steadily managing things like your growth, mood, and metabolism.

question: When is the best time to use a multiple line graph?

options.A: When displaying the exact percentages of a single pie chart
options.B: When comparing two or more related trends on the same set of axes
options.C: When listing text instructions for wound dressing changes
options.D: When only a single measurement is taken once in a lifetime

explanation: Correct! When you want to see how two or more groups stack up against each other over the same period, put them on one graph.

question: Which special structure helps single-unit smooth muscle cells contract together as one coordinated sheet?

options.A: Neuromuscular spindles
options.B: Desmosomes
options.C: Dense bodies
options.D: Gap junctions

explanation: Gap junctions act like open doorways between neighboring cells, letting electrical messages zip right through so they all squeeze together in harmony.

question: What is the true foundation of evidence-based practice in nursing?

options.A: Following the personal opinions of senior administrative staff
options.B: Using the cheapest medical supplies available on the market
options.C: Strict adherence to traditional hospital routines
options.D: Combining best research evidence with clinical expertise and patient values

explanation: You've got it! Evidence-based practice is a sweet spot: it blends what science proves works, your clinical skills as a nurse, and what the patient actually wants. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why should a female teen still use condoms even if she is already taking birth control pills?

options.A: Pills do not protect against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Condoms make hormonal pills absorb faster in the stomach
options.C: Using both methods doubles the hormonal protection level
options.D: Birth control pills stop working if taken without barrier methods

explanation: Exactly! Birth control pills are great for preventing pregnancy, but they do nothing against STIs. Condoms cover that gap. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h3)

question: How does the cerebellum use an 'efference copy' during a voluntary movement?

options.A: To produce neurotransmitters required for neuromuscular transmission
options.B: To directly contract skeletal muscles without involving the cortex
options.C: To store long-term procedural memories of past movements
options.D: To compare intended motor commands with actual sensory feedback

explanation: An efference copy is like a duplicate draft of the brain's movement plan sent to the cerebellum so it can check: 'Did our body actually do what we wanted it to do?' Brilliant nursing brain at work!

question: What kind of tissue mainly lines the inside of your nose and sinus cavities?

options.A: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium
options.B: Non-ciliated transitional epithelium
options.C: Simple cuboidal glandular epithelium
options.D: Stratified squamous keratinized epithelium

explanation: Think of this lining as your nose's natural broom and filter system! It has tiny hair-like cilia and sticky mucus that trap dust and germs so they don't reach your lungs. You've got this!

question: What is a major danger of misusing drugs in healthcare settings?

options.A: Immediate reduction in the overall cost of running hospitals
options.B: Development of antimicrobial resistance to common infections
options.C: Faster recovery times for patients with chronic illnesses
options.D: Decreased workload for nurses on the hospital wards

explanation: When we overuse antibiotics, germs learn how to fight back and survive, making common infections much harder to treat later.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major social determinant of health in Nigeria?

options.A: Availability of clean water and rural infrastructure
options.B: The brand of stethoscope used by attending physicians
options.C: Maternal education and literacy rates
options.D: Household income and overall poverty levels

explanation: Medical equipment brand does not determine public health outcomes, whereas income, education, and water supply profoundly affect community well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: In traditional Nigerian society, who has mainly taken care of older adults needing support?

options.A: Government-run hospitals
options.B: Non-profit religious charities
options.C: Extended family networks
options.D: Private nursing homes

explanation: You got this! Culturally, our extended family system has always been the primary safety net for caring for our aging loved ones.

question: What is a key advocacy duty for a nurse working to end FGM?

options.A: Keeping quiet about the practice to avoid offending elders
options.B: Educating communities and protecting girls at risk
options.C: Performing modified procedures to satisfy cultural demands safely
options.D: Reporting every adult survivor to the police for prosecution

explanation: Nurses serve as educators and champions by raising awareness and shielding young girls from harm before it happens. Another step closer to clinical excellence!

question: What is a major cause of cold-loving bacteria contaminating commercial milk?

options.A: Direct sunlight exposure during the transport phase
options.B: High levels of lactose found within the raw liquid
options.C: Improperly cleaned milking equipment and storage tanks
options.D: Natural vitamins added right after the milking process

explanation: Great thinking! When milking gear isn't washed properly, hidden films of bacteria build up and easily slip into the milk, even when it's kept cold.

question: Why do healthcare providers recommend breathable cotton underwear and loose clothing to prevent infections?

options.A: They increase local blood circulation to speed up tissue repair
options.B: They stop normal hormonal fluctuations from occurring
options.C: They prevent allergic reactions to harsh laundry detergents
options.D: They reduce moisture and heat buildup that encourages fungal growth

explanation: Yeast and bad bacteria love warm, dark, sweaty spaces. Breathable fabrics keep things cool, dry, and healthy! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h7)

question: A recovering leprosy patient feels very depressed because people in the community are avoiding them. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise them to pack up and relocate to another state
options.B: Assure them that people will soon forget about it
options.C: Offer a listening ear and connect them with a support group
options.D: Tell the patient never to discuss their illness with anyone

explanation: Emotional support and connecting with others who understand are powerful ways to beat stigma and heal the mind. You're going to be a wonderfully empathetic nurse!

question: Why do foetal lungs get only a tiny fraction of the body's blood supply?

options.A: They are completely absent during the first two trimesters
options.B: They are blocked by the growing liver tissue
options.C: They are filled with fluid and have high resistance
options.D: They receive all their oxygen directly from the mother's skin

explanation: Uninflated lungs full of amniotic fluid naturally push back against blood flow, so most blood finds easier alternate routes. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: Which muscle in the bladder wall is the main target for anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Sphincter muscle
options.B: Trigone muscle
options.C: Detrusor muscle
options.D: Ureteral smooth muscle

explanation: Anticholinergics work directly on the detrusor muscle to calm it down and stop involuntary bladder squeezes. You've got this!

question: Which of these is NOT a main job of the gonads?

options.A: Quickly fixing sudden drops in blood pressure
options.B: Supporting secondary sex traits like body hair
options.C: Helping with reproductive growth
options.D: Producing sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone

explanation: Spot on! Gonads focus on reproductive hormones. Blood pressure is managed by other organs like your kidneys and heart.

question: What is the main feature of polycythaemia?

options.A: A dangerous drop in blood platelets
options.B: A sudden drop in white blood cells
options.C: An abnormal increase in red blood cells
options.D: Too much fluid loss from blood vessels

explanation: You've got this! Polycythaemia simply means an overproduction of red blood cells in the body.

question: Which muscle is a safe, standard site for giving an intramuscular DMPA injection?

options.A: Gastrocnemius muscle
options.B: Ventrogluteal muscle
options.C: Rectus abdominis muscle
options.D: Internal oblique muscle

explanation: The ventrogluteal site is a fantastic choice because it has a thick muscle mass safely away from major nerves and blood vessels.

question: What extra job does propylthiouracil (PTU) do that methimazole doesn't?

options.A: Stimulating the pituitary gland to stop releasing TSH
options.B: Binding directly to circulating T3 molecules in the blood
options.C: Destroying existing thyroid tissue through direct radiation
options.D: Inhibiting the peripheral conversion of T4 into T3

explanation: Besides stopping new hormone production, PTU also slows down how T4 turns into the active T3 hormone in the body's tissues.

question: A patient asks how doctors will know for sure if a brain tumor is cancerous. What procedure gives the definitive diagnosis?

options.A: Routine eye examination
options.B: Tissue biopsy
options.C: Neurological reflex test
options.D: Blood cell count

explanation: You nailed it! A biopsy is the gold standard. By looking at actual tumor cells under a microscope, pathologists can tell for sure if it's cancerous and figure out its grade.

question: Which organ system is the hero for excreting non-volatile (fixed) metabolic acids from the body?

options.A: The lungs
options.B: The kidneys
options.C: The liver
options.D: The stomach

explanation: While the lungs handle volatile acids like $CO_2$, the kidneys take care of the heavy lifting by filtering out fixed metabolic acids in the urine.

question: What major upper reproductive tract condition can happen if cervicitis is left untreated?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Endometriosis of the bowel
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)

explanation: If lower tract infections aren't cleared, they can creep upward and turn into pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

question: Which vitamins are most easily lost when vegetables are boiled in too much water?

options.A: Inert plant fibers like cellulose and lignin
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins like vitamin C and B vitamins
options.C: Fat-soluble vitamins like vitamin A and vitamin E
options.D: Structural minerals like calcium and iron

explanation: You got it! Vitamins C and B love water, so they dissolve right out of the veggies and into the cooking pot.

question: What is the go-to emergency medication for a patient in acute anaphylactic shock?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Salbutamol inhaler
options.C: Diphenhydramine
options.D: Hydrocortisone

explanation: Epinephrine is a lifesaver in anaphylaxis! It quickly tightens blood vessels, opens up tight airways, and keeps the heart pumping.

question: As a nurse, what is one of the best ways you can help stop drug resistance?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum drugs for every common viral cold
options.B: Educating patients to finish their entire antibiotic prescription
options.C: Stopping medication immediately once mild symptoms disappear
options.D: Encouraging patients to save leftover pills for future sickness

explanation: You got it! Always remind patients to complete their meds. Stopping early leaves the toughest germs alive to breed stronger, resistant generations.

question: What is a key nursing duty when checking a pregnant patient's skin?

options.A: Differentiating harmless body changes from serious medical conditions
options.B: Telling the patient to ignore any skin changes until after delivery
options.C: Reporting all common stretch marks to the primary surgeon
options.D: Prescribing strong steroid creams to cure all rashes instantly

explanation: You are the frontline! Knowing the difference between normal pregnancy glow-ups and warning signs like cholestasis makes you an awesome nurse.

question: What is the difference between a normal drug side effect and an adverse drug reaction (ADR)?

options.A: It is completely harmless and requires no intervention
options.B: It is a harmful and unintended response at normal doses
options.C: It is always an expected pharmacological outcome
options.D: It only happens when a patient takes an overdose

explanation: Think of an ADR as an unwanted, harmful surprise that happens even when you give the exact right dose. You've got this!

question: Which disease is most commonly caught through accidental needle stick injuries in the clinic?

options.A: Malaria
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Typhoid fever
options.D: Hepatitis B

explanation: Hepatitis B is very easily spread through contaminated sharps in the hospital. This is why safety with needles is a huge deal for every nurse!

question: What is the main reason to teach an osteoarthritis patient about 'activity pacing'?

options.A: To ensure the patient finishes all chores before morning stiffness starts
options.B: To eliminate all physical movement from their daily routine
options.C: To balance rest periods with tasks and protect joints from overuse
options.D: To prevent the need for any future medical evaluations

explanation: Correct! Pacing helps patients get their daily tasks done without pushing their joints too hard and causing extra pain.

question: What is one of the biggest benefits of placing a newborn directly on the mother's bare chest (skin-to-skin contact) right after birth?

options.A: It helps stabilize the infant's temperature and blood sugar
options.B: It prevents the mother from experiencing afterpains
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of newborn jaundice
options.D: It guarantees the infant will latch without any assistance

explanation: Skin-to-skin is magical! The mother's body acts like a natural incubator, helping the baby's breathing, temperature, and blood sugar stay steady.

question: A patient suddenly crashes in the ward, and the nurse in charge immediately takes control and gives clear, fast orders to everyone. What leadership style is this?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Laissez-faire
options.C: Servant
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: In emergencies, an autocratic style saves lives! It ensures everyone moves fast and coordinates without wasting time debating.

question: How do water-soluble vitamins behave differently from fat-soluble vitamins in the body?

options.A: Water-soluble vitamins can be stored in the liver in large toxic amounts
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins play no role in normal human physiological processes
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine and require more frequent intake
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins cannot be absorbed without adequate daily hydration

explanation: You're doing great! Water-soluble vitamins dissolve in body fluids, meaning any extra gets peed out. That's why we need a fresh supply of them regularly in our meals.

question: Why do patients in areas with few clinics feel extra pressured to stay quiet?

options.A: They receive free private insurance coverage
options.B: They prefer substandard medical equipment
options.C: They have few alternative clinics to go to if they are mistreated
options.D: They are legally forbidden from speaking to nurses

explanation: You got it! When there's nowhere else to go for care, patients feel too dependent to risk upsetting the staff.

question: What do vitamins A, C, and E mainly do for your skin?

options.A: Increasing the overall thickness of the subcutaneous fat layer
options.B: Acting as primary cleansers for the epidermal surface
options.C: Directly producing melanin to determine skin color
options.D: Acting as antioxidants to protect cells from oxidative stress

explanation: Spot on! These vitamins act like little bodyguards, fighting off nasty molecules that try to damage your skin cells.

question: What is the primary goal of family planning counselling?

options.A: Ensuring every client chooses modern barrier methods
options.B: Reducing the overall birth rate in rural communities
options.C: Convincing every client to use permanent surgical methods
options.D: Helping clients make free and informed reproductive choices

explanation: Counselling empowers clients to make voluntary decisions about their own families rather than forcing a specific choice upon them. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h1)

question: Why is it so important to keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat foods in the kitchen?

options.A: To make cleaning the counter easier
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
options.C: To keep different food flavors from mixing
options.D: To make the meat cook faster in the pot

explanation: Exactly! We separate them to stop bacteria from jumping onto foods that won't be cooked again. Basic kitchen hygiene is great patient education!

question: Which term describes a complete loss of feeling or touch sensation in a part of the body?

options.A: Hypesthesia
options.B: Paresthesia
options.C: Analgesia
options.D: Anesthesia

explanation: Anesthesia means total absence of feeling. You'll hear this word in surgery too, where patients are given drugs to block all sensation!

question: How is an adverse drug reaction that leads to death or permanent disability classified?

options.A: Mild
options.B: Expected
options.C: Tolerance
options.D: Severe

explanation: Reactions causing permanent damage, hospitalization, or death are classified as severe and require immediate reporting to keep others safe.

question: Why do nurses study pharmacology instead of just memorizing drug names?

options.A: To anticipate clinical problems and evaluate patient responses safely
options.B: To manufacture synthetic compounds in the hospital pharmacy
options.C: To write safe prescriptions independently without a doctor
options.D: To replace the clinical pharmacist during night shifts

explanation: Knowing your drugs helps you spot side effects early and keep your patients safe. You are building vital clinical instincts!

question: You are caring for a 38-week pregnant mother with many past deliveries who also has severe anemia. What is the best delivery recommendation?

options.A: Advise delivery at a well-equipped hospital that has blood transfusion services.
options.B: Wait for spontaneous labor at home until contractions are very close.
options.C: Plan a home birth attended by a traditional birth attendant.
options.D: Encourage unassisted labor to avoid medical interventions.

explanation: Because she has a high risk of heavy bleeding and low blood count, she needs to deliver where doctors and nurses can easily give blood or emergency care.

question: What is the first step when preparing to share serious news using the SPIKES protocol?

options.A: Setting up a private, quiet space with minimal interruptions
options.B: Giving the patient all test results immediately upon entering
options.C: Asking the family to leave the room for privacy
options.D: Reading the patient's vital signs out loud

explanation: The first step of SPIKES focuses on setting, which involves arranging a private, comfortable environment for the discussion. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the main job of the registered nurse inside a healthcare team?

options.A: Replacing the dietician for meal planning and kitchen duties.
options.B: Providing all physical therapy exercises without therapist assistance.
options.C: Prescribing new medications when the doctor is off duty.
options.D: Acting as the clinical hub to coordinate care among all disciplines.

explanation: As nurses, we bring the whole healthcare team together so everyone is on the same page for the patient's care. You're mastering teamwork!

question: An instructor wants to use adult learning principles when teaching IV cannulation. What's the best way to do it?

options.A: Show how the skill solves immediate clinical problems students will face on the ward
options.B: Require students to memorize the history of intravenous therapy before practice
options.C: Ignore student past experiences because healthcare changes too fast
options.D: Use strict punishments and pop quizzes to force compliance with the protocol

explanation: Adults learn best when they see the immediate, practical value of a skill for real-life patient care. Connecting it to ward duties makes it click!

question: A patient diagnosed with active Lassa fever is admitted to a special ward. What infection control action is this?

options.A: Isolation
options.B: Surveillance
options.C: Immunization
options.D: Quarantine

explanation: Separating a person who already has an active disease diagnosis is classified as isolation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the main job of your nasal cavity when you breathe in air?

options.A: To store excess air during heavy exercise
options.B: To produce sound waves for vocalization
options.C: To exchange oxygen directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To warm, humidify, and filter incoming air

explanation: Spot on! Your nose acts like a natural air conditioner, warming, cleaning, and moistening the air before it travels down into your lungs.

question: When do you typically hook up a humidification bottle filled with sterile water to an oxygen setup?

options.A: Only when the patient is diagnosed with an active lung infection
options.B: Whenever oxygen is delivered at any flow rate below one liter
options.C: When delivering higher flow rates that can dry the nasal passages
options.D: To cool the temperature of the gas before it enters the nose

explanation: Medical oxygen is very dry and can irritate the nose at higher flows. Adding sterile water for humidification keeps your patient nice and comfortable!

question: Which social factor is consistently proven to help young girls delay marriage and early childbearing?

options.A: Traditional community ceremonies
options.B: Living in an urban city center
options.C: Access to formal education
options.D: Employment in the agricultural sector

explanation: Education is a powerful tool! When girls stay in school, they gain knowledge, open up better life opportunities, and naturally delay marriage and childbearing.

question: A patient taking warfarin has a dangerously high INR and mild bleeding. What will the medical team most likely give?

options.A: Aspirin
options.B: Iron tablets
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Heparin

explanation: Since warfarin blocks Vitamin K, giving extra Vitamin K is the direct antidote to reverse its effects and restore normal clotting.

question: A patient with high blood pressure stops taking their antihypertensive drugs because they feel fine. What is the most likely outcome of this action?

options.A: The body permanently adjusts and cures the hypertension naturally
options.B: The liver will start producing its own natural blood pressure medicine
options.C: Blood pressure will stay normal as long as the patient eats well
options.D: The patient remains at high risk for silent organ damage and stroke

explanation: Hypertension is a chronic condition managed, not cured, by medications. Stopping treatment causes blood pressure to rise again, silently damaging vital organs like the heart and brain. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why do we perform Leopold's maneuvers when a pregnant woman is admitted?

options.A: To determine the fetal position and presentation
options.B: To measure the mother's blood pressure accurately
options.C: To check if the amniotic fluid is clear or meconium-stained
options.D: To measure the exact cervical dilation in centimeters

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are just our hands-on way of feeling the mum's tummy to figure out how the baby is lying inside.

question: A patient comes in with a high fever and body aches. What important detail should you ask about first?

options.A: Recent travel and possible mosquito bites
options.B: Their family heart disease history
options.C: When they last visited the dentist
options.D: What vitamins they take daily

explanation: Spot on! Always check for local vector exposures like mosquitoes when dealing with fevers in our environment.

question: What is a main purpose of a family planning referral?

options.A: To permanently punish clients who miss their clinic appointments
options.B: To reduce the total number of people using modern contraceptives
options.C: To transfer financial responsibility for drugs to the client
options.D: To connect clients with specialized care when needed

explanation: Referrals are primarily designed to link clients to the specific level of care required for their health status. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h2)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction?

options.A: Lower back pain and dark urine
options.B: Dry cough and sudden hair loss
options.C: Gradual joint stiffness and swelling
options.D: Severe itching and localized rash

explanation: When red blood cells break down rapidly inside the body, the released hemoglobin travels to the kidneys and bloodstream, leading to classic flank/lower back pain and dark, tea-colored urine.

question: Why should you tell a patient to avoid clearing their throat aggressively right after a laryngoscopy?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from writing the final discharge summary.
options.B: It increases the patient's blood pressure and heart rate significantly.
options.C: It forces the residual topical spray down into the stomach too fast.
options.D: It can cause trauma or irritation to the recently numbed vocal cords.

explanation: Spot on! Since the vocal cords are still a bit sleepy and vulnerable, harsh throat clearing can easily bruise or injure them.

question: What is the main reason nurses use medical eligibility guidelines during family planning counseling?

options.A: To test the client for sexually transmitted infections in the lab
options.B: To calculate the exact cost of the supplies for the client
options.C: To determine the religious beliefs of the client's family
options.D: To screen for health conditions that make specific methods unsafe

explanation: Safety first! These guidelines help us spot health issues like high blood pressure that could make certain hormones risky. Excellent nursing care!

question: What is the correct action a nurse should take before applying a new dose of a topical skin cream?

options.A: Shave all body hair from the area regardless of the medication type
options.B: Scrub the skin hard with alcohol wipes to remove the stratum corneum
options.C: Gently clean the skin to remove old medication residue and dirt
options.D: Apply a thick layer of plastic wrap over the old cream without cleaning

explanation: Cleaning away old residue and debris ensures proper contact and prevents chemical buildup or irritation on the skin surface. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h6)

question: How did Nigerian mothers traditionally space their children before modern contraceptives arrived?

options.A: Daily ingestion of synthetic hormone pills
options.B: Intrauterine copper device insertion
options.C: Surgical tubal ligation procedures
options.D: Prolonged breastfeeding and postpartum abstinence

explanation: Traditional Nigerian societies used natural, reliable spacing methods like extended breastfeeding and resting from sex after childbirth.

question: Which viral infection is most commonly linked globally to unsafe injections?

options.A: Hepatitis B Virus
options.B: Influenza Virus
options.C: Varicella Zoster
options.D: Rhinovirus

explanation: Well done! Along with Hepatitis C and HIV, Hepatitis B is one of the main bloodborne pathogens spread when injection safety rules are broken. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h2)

question: What percentage of weight loss from pre-pregnancy weight helps nurses identify hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Loss of exactly 2 percent of body weight
options.B: Loss of more than 5 percent of body weight
options.C: Loss of up to 1 percent of body weight
options.D: Loss of 1 to 3 percent of body weight

explanation: Dropping more than 5% of her original body weight is a key sign that a mom-to-be has moved past normal morning sickness into severe hyperemesis. You've got this!

question: What is the main reason regulatory bodies like the NMCN oversee nursing practice?

options.A: To protect the public from substandard practice and ensure legal compliance
options.B: To fund the construction of private residential houses
options.C: To supply free medications directly to nursing homes
options.D: To handle international travel arrangements for nurses

explanation: Regulatory bodies exist to set clear professional boundaries, ensuring every nurse maintains safe standards to protect the public. Great job!

question: What is the most common immediate complication to watch for after a male circumcision?

options.A: Hemorrhage
options.B: Total urinary retention
options.C: Erectile dysfunction
options.D: Meatal stenosis

explanation: Because the male genital area has a rich blood supply, bleeding (hemorrhage) is the most frequent acute thing to monitor for right after the procedure.

question: What key stage of a parasite's life cycle happens inside its definitive host?

options.A: The parasite reaches maturity and reproduces sexually
options.B: The parasite dies off because the immune system is too strong
options.C: The parasite transforms directly into an ectoparasite
options.D: The parasite only undergoes brief larval resting stages

explanation: You're doing great! The definitive host is the VIP lounge for the parasite—it's where they finally grow up into adults and reproduce.

question: A patient is healing from surgery and needs to build new tissue. Which process is at work?

options.A: Anabolism, because it builds complex tissues using energy
options.B: Hemolysis, because it breaks down red blood cells for iron
options.C: Osmosis, because it balances electrolytes in the blood
options.D: Catabolism, because it destroys old cells to provide water

explanation: Anabolism is all about building up! It uses energy to knit tissues back together and help your patients heal up nicely.

question: Which group of people benefits the most from herd immunity against respiratory infections?

options.A: Young adults working in busy office buildings
options.B: Older adults who get their flu shots on time
options.C: People who are too young or have weak immune systems to get vaccines
options.D: Healthy athletes training outdoors

explanation: Herd immunity acts like a protective shield. When most of the community is vaccinated, it stops the germ from spreading to vulnerable people who cannot take vaccines themselves.

question: A breastfeeding mother who delivered six weeks ago asks for a contraceptive implant. What should you tell her?

options.A: She must first undergo a liver biopsy to prove her body can tolerate the progestin hormone
options.B: She is completely ineligible because implants will immediately dry up her breast milk supply
options.C: She is eligible, as progestin-only implants do not interfere with milk production and are safe during breastfeeding
options.D: She must wait until her baby is at least one year old before any hormonal method can be discussed

explanation: Great news for new mums! Progestin-only options are safe during breastfeeding and won't mess with her milk supply.

question: Why can taking a health history for hormone problems be tricky for a nurse?

options.A: Symptoms are usually vague and overlap across different disorders
options.B: Patients almost never remember when their symptoms started
options.C: Endocrine problems only affect one specific body system at a time
options.D: Laboratory tests are completely useless without a physical exam

explanation: You got it! Hormonal issues often start with everyday complaints like constant tiredness, making it hard to pin down the exact cause without patient probing.

question: Which vaccine is super important to give if a client has a fresh, unsterilized scarification wound?

options.A: BCG tuberculosis
options.B: Tetanus toxoid
options.C: Oral polio vaccine
options.D: Yellow fever shot

explanation: Spot on! Cuts made with non-sterile tools carry a high risk of tetanus, making a booster shot a vital life-saving step.

question: What usually happens when someone skips meals all day and eats one massive meal at night?

options.A: Blood sugar spikes and digestive strain
options.B: Lower nighttime blood pressure
options.C: Faster weight loss and improved metabolism
options.D: Better absorption of essential vitamins

explanation: Good to know! Overloading the stomach all at once confuses digestion and causes sudden jumps and crashes in blood sugar.

question: When a heart valve is narrowed and blocked, what kind of extra strain does it put on the heart?

options.A: Electrical overload
options.B: Perfusion overload
options.C: Volume overload
options.D: Pressure overload

explanation: When a valve is narrowed, the heart has to push much harder to squeeze blood through it. That extra resistance creates a pressure overload!

question: Which bleeding pattern is a serious warning sign (red flag) after a medical abortion?

options.A: Passing a single clot the size of a coin
options.B: Spotting that lasts for up to three weeks
options.C: Bleeding that stops completely after 24 hours
options.D: Soaking through two large pads per hour for two hours

explanation: You're doing great! Soaking through two large pads every hour for two hours straight is too much—it's a red flag that needs prompt medical evaluation.

question: Why is it important for the baby to keep moving downward steadily during labour?

options.A: It allows all other cardinal movements to occur successfully
options.B: It stops maternal contractions from becoming too painful
options.C: It immediately closes the cervix after the baby passes
options.D: It prevents the placenta from detaching too early

explanation: Exactly! Continuous downward movement helps the baby's head touch the pelvic floor, triggering all the other cool turns and movements needed for birth.

question: A manager wants to introduce a new clinical audit system with minimal staff pushback. What is the best approach?

options.A: Install hidden security cameras in the nurses' station without telling anyone
options.B: Threatened immediate termination for anyone who questions the audit schedule
options.C: Involve frontline nurses in designing the standards and explain the safety benefits
options.D: Keep all performance data completely secret from the nursing staff

explanation: When you involve staff in the process, they build trust, feel valued, and truly understand why the safety controls matter.

question: A patient who lost their job six months ago visits the clinic complaining of constant headaches and stomach aches with no clear medical cause. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A rare genetic blood disorder
options.B: An acute bacterial infection
options.C: A reaction to routine childhood immunizations
options.D: Somatic symptoms of underlying psychological stress

explanation: Spot on! People facing job loss often express emotional distress through physical aches, known as somatic symptoms. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h2)

question: Why don't we pull back (aspirate) on the plunger anymore for routine subcutaneous shots like insulin?

options.A: It makes the medication completely inactive in the syringe
options.B: It increases the risk of the needle breaking in the skin
options.C: It causes unnecessary tissue trauma and increases bruising
options.D: It causes the plunger to stick permanently inside the barrel

explanation: Modern practice shows that the chance of hitting a vessel here is tiny. Pulling back just causes extra discomfort and bruising for no real benefit.
